body_ar: شرع الله سبحانه لعبادة شرائع الدين، وأكدها وبينها رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن هذه الشرائع صلة الأرحام، فمن وصلها وأدى حقها وصله الله ورضي عنه، وكان ذلك سبباً في زيادة عمره وبركة رزقه، ومن قطعها وأهمل حقها قطعه الله، وقطع نسله ورزقه. الأدلة الدالة على الإحسان إلى ذوي القربى وصلة الرحم: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه، واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى شرع لعباده شرائع الدين، وأكدها وبينها رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وألزم عباده باتباعها، وحظهم على الأخذ بها إيجاباً وسلباً، فالإيجاب بالترغيب في اتباعها، والسلب في الترهيب من مخالفتها، ومن هذه الشرائع التي شرعها الله لعباده وارتضاها لهم: شريعة صلة الأرحام، إنها شريعة عظيمة، ذات مكانة عظيمة في هذا الدين الذي جاء به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من عند الله تعالى..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, glorified is He, prescribed for His servants the ordinances of the religion, and His Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — confirmed them and made them plain. Among these ordinances is the maintaining of the ties of kinship. Whoever maintains them and discharges their due, God maintains His bond with him and is pleased with him, and this is a cause of his lifespan being lengthened and his provision blessed; and whoever severs them and neglects their due, God severs him, and severs his progeny and his provision.

## The evidence indicating kindness to close relatives and the maintaining of the ties of kinship

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, prescribed for His servants the ordinances of the religion, and His Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — confirmed them and made them plain; and He bound His servants to follow them and urged them to take them up, both positively and negatively — positively, by encouragement to follow them; negatively, by warning against departing from them. Among these ordinances which God prescribed for His servants and was pleased with for them is the ordinance of maintaining the ties of kinship. It is a mighty ordinance, of great standing in this religion which the Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — brought from God Most High..

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis exactly where the heading's subject — the evidence — would begin; not a single piece of evidence is given. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/c-a-18.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words. Here the two voices overlap unusually closely: the transcribed opening repeats the synopsis's first sentence almost word for word, which suggests the synopsis was written by lifting the lesson's own opening rather than composed separately.

flags.arabic: فمن وصلها وأدى حقها وصله الله ... ومن قطعها وأهمل حقها قطعه الله، وقطع نسله ورزقه
flags.context: the consequences set out in the site's synopsis
options: render exactly, and attribute to the synopsis rather than to the Sheikh
attribute the statement to the Sheikh
flags.note: These are substantive claims — that maintaining kinship lengthens life and blesses provision, and that severing it brings God's severing of one's progeny and provision — and they draw on well-known prophetic reports. They fall entirely inside the site's synopsis; the transcribed portion of the lesson breaks off before any of it. No narrator, collection or grading is given and none has been added. These sentences must not be catalogued as the Sheikh's own statement.

flags.arabic: شرع الله سبحانه لعبادة شرائع الدين ... وحظهم على الأخذ بها
flags.context: two orthographic slips, one in the synopsis and one in the transcription
options: read 'لعبادة' as 'لعباده' (for His servants) and 'وحظهم' as 'وحثهم' (and urged them), and leave both as served
flags.note: 'لعبادة' has a tāʾ marbūṭah where 'لعباده' is required — the transcribed portion two sentences later has the correct form in the same phrase, which settles it. 'وحظهم' has a ẓāʾ where 'وحثهم' is required by the sense. Both left as served in body_ar and read as intended in the English, recorded rather than silently corrected.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
'شريعة' is rendered 'ordinance' throughout rather than 'law' or 'Sharia', because the record uses it of one particular prescribed practice among many, not of the legal system as a whole.

No ruling term appears anywhere in the record; 'ألزم' is rendered 'bound' rather than given one of the five renderings, since it describes God's binding of His servants generally and not the grading of a specific act.
